subject: Vendor decision readout and next tests
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@nexacapital.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor decision readout and next tests

Laura — thanks for taking the time this morning. Short recap from our side plus proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key pain you reiterated:
- Unpredictable inference costs as usage spikes during market close windows.
- Occasional tail latency outliers (esp. >8s p95) that break downstream realtime rules.
- Need an isolated environment for audit reasons (data residency + log retention settings).

Goals you stated:
- Keep median latency under 120ms and p95 under 800ms for routing use cases.
- Reduce per-token spend for embeddings/generation by at least 30% vs your current provider.
- Validate audit logs and KMS integration for a proof-of-compliance run.

Today's readout (what we showed):
- Quantized variant + smart batching reduced token cost on a synthetic spike by ~28% in our lab.
- Live demo of fallback routing that keeps throughput when a model tier is saturated.
- Walkthrough of Private deployment controls (audit log export, KMS).

Open decision factors you flagged for the internal committee:
1) True p95 under representative traffic (you want a run against a 48-hour business-close replay).
2) Quantization effects on your proprietary post-processing pipeline — prefer a test with your model artifacts.
3) Contractual SLAs for burst capacity and credits.

Proposed next tests (we recommend):
- 48-hour replay on your sample trace with our dedicated pool (we’ll produce p50/p95/TCP histograms).
- A short A/B where 20% of calls use quantized model variant with your post-processing chain — compare logits drift and output diff metrics.
- KMS + log export verification into your staging account; 1-week retention snapshot for audit review.

Owner / timeline (proposed):
- Redwood sets up dedicated test pool & initial config (Marcus) — target: Nov 6 start.
- Aditya to run the quantized A/B and produce artifact diff report — deliverable Nov 9.
- Vanessa to draft a short mutual action plan and T&Cs summary for burst credits — deliverable Nov 5.

Attachments: I’ll attach a lightweight vendor comparison matrix and the proposed MVP test plan after we confirm — attaching in follow-up.

Ask: Can you confirm the two artifacts you said you could share for the tests: 1) the 48-hour traffic trace (anonymized) and 2) the post-processing container image name + access? If we get those by end of day Wed Nov 4, we can start the replay on Nov 6 as proposed.

Thanks again — we’ll keep the comms tight.

—
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0191

From: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@nexacapital.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Vendor decision readout and next tests

Marcus — thanks for the concise summary, that matches what we heard internally. A few clarifications so the test scope is right: 

1) 48-hour trace: we can provide Nov 1–2 anonymized trace (will strip account ids). Expect ~15M requests, mixed realtime and batched inference. Delivery ETA: COB Wed Nov 4.
2) Post-processing: we don’t run anything proprietary inside the model. The concern is deterministic tokenization + a light scoring filter (container image: registry.nexa.internal/postproc:v2.1). We will grant read-only registry access to the redwood-test service account.
3) SLA credit ask: our procurement will push for a 99.9% p95 SLA with a small credit ladder for burst failures. They understand some caveats for root-cause but want a clear plan.

On the quantization A/B: we want output fidelity metrics that include your token-level edit distance scoring and a short human review sample for anything where the score drops below 0.92.

We’re OK with the proposed start dates. Vanessa — thanks for taking the lead on the MAP/terms summary.

Laura
Head of Infrastructure | Nexa Capital
laura.simmons@nexacapital.com | +1 212-555-0147

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor decision readout and next tests

+1 — looping internal notes and quick plan. Quoting Laura below for context.

On Tue, 3 Nov 2026 at 13:22, Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@nexacapital.com> wrote:
> Marcus — thanks for the concise summary, that matches what we heard internally. A few clarifications so the test scope is right:
>
> 1) 48-hour trace: we can provide Nov 1–2 anonymized trace (will strip account ids). Delivery ETA: COB Wed Nov 4.
> 2) Post-processing: we don’t run anything proprietary inside the model. The concern is deterministic tokenization + a light scoring filter (container image: registry.nexa.internal/postproc:v2.1). We will grant read-only registry access to the redwood-test service account.
> 3) SLA credit ask: our procurement will push for a 99.9% p95 SLA with a small credit ladder for burst failures. They understand some caveats for root-cause but want a clear plan.

Internal action items (who does what):
- Aditya: prepare quantization A/B harness that can accept their postproc container and emit token-level edit-distance plus a human-sample queue. Target: run by Nov 6–8 and report Nov 9. (Aditya, confirm you can take registry read-only creds and the container mount plan.)
- Marcus: confirm dedicated pool sizing for 15M reqs over 48h and config the replay harness. I’ll need the expected concurrency numbers (requests/sec breakdown) — Marcus to grab from Laura trace doc when it lands.
- Vanessa: draft MAP + short vendor comparison matrix highlighting risk delta between options (fallback policies, private deploy controls, cost delta). Deliverable: Nov 5 EOD.

Risk flags to capture in the matrix:
- Quantization-induced downstream drift on scoring thresholds
- Log retention and queryability for audit (need to validate query SLA)
- Burst capacity ramp timing and credit eligibility windows

Aditya — I’ll attach a skeleton A/B harness spec (see drive link) and drop the readme in the hubspot deal.

—Vanessa
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0188

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor decision readout and next tests — confirmed start dates and attachments

Laura — thanks and appreciated. Confirming the plan and next steps with attachments.

Deliverables we’ll start Nov 6 (as discussed):
- Redwood will provision a dedicated test pool configured for the 48-hour replay. I configured a baseline to handle peak concurrency up to 800 RPS (we can scale during the run).
- Aditya will run the quantized A/B against the postproc container you provide; he’ll seed a human-review queue for any outputs below 0.92.
- Vanessa will share the MAP + the vendor comparison matrix with procurement language.

Attachments included: 20261103-vendor-matrix.xlsx (snapshot comparison with risk notes) and 20261103-mvp-test-plan.pdf (detailed test steps, success criteria, and telemetry we’ll deliver).

Small asks for access: 
1) Please share container registry read-only credentials for registry.nexa.internal/postproc:v2.1 to redwood-test@redwood-ci (we’ll only pull, no writes).
2) Upload the anonymized 48-hour trace to the Drive link I shared earlier (or send via sftp if you prefer).

Timing: if we receive artifacts by COB Nov 4 we will start Nov 6 and post a first-run summary by Nov 9. Procurement lane (SLA credits) — Vanessa will draft a proposal and we’ll coordinate with your procurement.

If that all sounds good I’ll mark the HubSpot deal RDW-2026-374 as "tests-scheduled" and begin provisioning.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—
Marcus Lin
